rubrics.evidence: The agent patch deletes the shared `__HelperContext` interface from tslib.d.ts and reverts the helper signatures to `object`/`any`. In tslib.es6.js, tslib.es6.mjs, and tslib.js it removes `provideHelperCapability`/`createHelperContext` and every `createHelperContext(...)` call from `__generator`, `__values`, `__asyncGenerator`, `__asyncDelegator`, `__asyncValues`, `__addDisposableResource`, and `__disposeResources`. The former shared capabilities are restored as nested functions local to the family that uses them (`accept` in `__esDecorate`, `awaitable` in `__asyncGenerator`, `settle` in `__asyncValues`), so no per-call record carries the cross-family adopt/awaitable/settle/accept/addInitializer kit.
rubrics.criterion: No helper family's per-call record carries members of a cross-family capability protocol that the family never reads, writes, or overrides: after the repair, each record-producing or record-consuming helper family (downlevel generator record, sync iterator adapter, async generator, async delegator, async-values adapter, decorator application contexts, and the two disposal-environment helpers) exposes on its records only capabilities that family itself exercises or its callers supply.

rubrics.evidence: In tslib.d.ts the agent deletes the shared `__HelperContext` interface and restores each signature to its own concrete/original annotation: `__esDecorate(... contextIn: object ...)`, `__generator(thisArg: any, body: Function): any`, `__values(o: any): any`, `__asyncGenerator(...): any`, `__asyncDelegator(o: any): any`, `__asyncValues(o: any): any`, `__addDisposableResource<T>(env: { stack: ...; error: unknown; hasError: boolean; }, ...)`, and `__disposeResources(env: { stack: ...; error: unknown; hasError: boolean; }): any`. No signature remains routed through the shared protocol.
rubrics.criterion: Every helper signature that was routed through the shared record protocol in the declaration file is annotated with a type that describes that helper's own record or input shape (a helper-specific interface, its original concrete annotation, or an equivalent narrow type), rather than one protocol shared across unrelated helper signatures.

rubrics.evidence: The patch deletes `createHelperContext`/`provideHelperCapability` and restores family-local glue: in `__esDecorate` a local `function accept(f) { ... }` is reintroduced and `addInitializer`/result validation call `accept(...)` instead of `context.accept`; in `__asyncGenerator` a local `function awaitable(finish, fail) { ... }` closure is added and `awaitReturn` calls it instead of `i.awaitable`; in `__asyncValues` a local `function settle(resolve, reject, done, value) { ... }` is added and `verb` calls `settle(...)` instead of `i.settle`. `createHelperContext` calls are also removed from `__generator`, `__values`, `__asyncDelegator`, `__addDisposableResource`, and `__disposeResources` across tslib.es6.js/mjs and tslib.js, and the `__HelperContext` interface is removed from tslib.d.ts.
rubrics.criterion: The behavior-carrying logic that the shared kit took over for three families is served by family-internal implementations again: decorator-result validation and the addInitializer enqueue in the decorator helper, the return-path promise wiring in the async generator, and the step settlement in the async-values adapter each resolve through code owned by that family (a local helper, closure, or family-local equivalent) rather than through members installed by a cross-family protocol.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch applies the same resolution to all three runtime copies: tslib.js, tslib.es6.js, and tslib.es6.mjs. In each file it removes the injected provideHelperCapability/createHelperContext block, restores local accept/awaitable/settle helper functions, reverts __generator/__values/__asyncGenerator/__asyncDelegator/__asyncValues to plain object construction, and removes createHelperContext calls from __addDisposableResource and __disposeResources. tslib.d.ts is also reverted consistently, removing __HelperContext and restoring object/any signatures, so all shipped copies match.
rubrics.criterion: The resolution is applied consistently to all three shipped runtime copies (the classic/UMD copy, the CommonJS copy, and the pure-ESM copy), so all three keep exporting the same names and any examination of one copy matches the corresponding helper in the others.

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes the `__HelperContext` interface entirely from tslib.d.ts and reverts every annotation back to `object`/`any`/the original `{ stack: ... }` shapes, so no declaration references the removed protocol type. In parallel, the runtime files delete `provideHelperCapability` and `createHelperContext`, remove all `createHelperContext(...)` calls from `__esDecorate`, `__generator`, `__values`, `__asyncGenerator`, `__asyncDelegator`, `__asyncValues`, `__addDisposableResource`, and `__disposeResources`, and restore local `accept`, `awaitable`, and `settle` functions. Both coupled surfaces are resolved together with no surviving `__HelperContext` references or wider protocol annotations.
rubrics.criterion: The runtime resolution and the declaration resolution land together: no declaration annotation survives that references a protocol type removed from the code, and no remaining annotation forces a wider record surface than the runtime provides.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch deletes the `__HelperContext` interface block from tslib.d.ts and reverts all signature references to `object`/`any`. In all three JS emission formats (tslib.js, tslib.es6.js, tslib.es6.mjs), the `provideHelperCapability` and `createHelperContext` definitions are removed entirely, and every call site (`__generator`, `__values`, `__asyncGenerator`, `__asyncDelegator`, `__asyncValues`, `__esDecorate`, `__addDisposableResource`, `__disposeResources`) no longer references them. rubrics.criterion: No scaffolding whose only purpose was to install or document the shared protocol is left behind: the kit functions, the capability-installation helper, or the interface block are deleted rather than left defined-and-unreferenced, in every emission format and in the declaration file.

rubrics.evidence: The patch deletes the `__HelperContext` interface and its doc block from tslib.d.ts, removes the `// Records produced by or handed to tslib helpers ... one uniform runtime surface` comment and `createHelperContext` from tslib.es6.js/tslib.es6.mjs/tslib.js, and changes the `__esDecorate` param doc from `__HelperContext record` to `The decorator context to clone...`. The only added comments describe family-local/private helpers (`accept`, `awaitable`, `settle`) and state they are internal/private and not exposed; none advertise a shared capability surface.
rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave explanatory comments or doc-comment blocks advertising the one-uniform-surface design (a shared capability surface adopted by every helper's records) attached to members that now expose family-local surfaces.

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes `createHelperContext` but rewires all three families so no call path reads a removed protocol member: in tslib.es6.js/mjs/js, `__esDecorate` reintroduces local `function accept` and calls `accept(result.get)`/`accept(result.set)`/`accept(result.init)` instead of `context.accept`; `__asyncGenerator` adds local `function awaitable` and `awaitReturn` calls `awaitable(f, reject)` instead of `i.awaitable`; `__asyncValues` adds local `function settle` and calls `settle(resolve, reject, v.done, v.value)` instead of `i.settle`. `__generator`, `__values`, `__asyncDelegator`, and the disposable helpers no longer wrap records with the removed kit.
rubrics.criterion: The repair does not break the promise-flavored families by leaving their call paths reading protocol members that no longer exist: consuming an async generator (including its return path), iterating with the async-values adapter, or applying a decorator must not raise a missing-member error (such as calling a capability that is no longer installed).

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes createHelperContext/provideHelperCapability entirely and stops adopting records into __HelperContext. __generator returns Object.create(...) directly, __values returns a plain {next:...} object, __asyncDelegator/__asyncValues return plain {}, __asyncGenerator uses a local awaitable function, __esDecorate uses a local accept function, and __addDisposableResource/__disposeResources no longer call createHelperContext(env). No helper-local glue is installed as own enumerable or non-enumerable members on returned records or disposal environments, so the enumeration surface is restored rather than changed.
rubrics.criterion: The repair does not change the enumeration surface of any helper-produced record as user code observes it: the member sets visible through for-in, Object.keys, and Object.getOwnPropertyNames on returned generator records, iterator adapters, async adapters, and decorator contexts stay the same as before, and the disposal environments handed to the tracking helpers keep accepting the same fields.

rubrics.evidence: The refactor request targets the shared capability kit that funneled per-call objects through __HelperContext. The agent patch removes __HelperContext from tslib.d.ts and restores broad signatures: __esDecorate's contextIn changes back to object, __addDisposableResource/__disposeResources env changes from __HelperContext & { stack...; error; hasError } to { stack...; error; hasError }, and __generator/__values/__asyncGenerator/__asyncDelegator/__asyncValues return types change from __HelperContext to any. These types are as broad as or broader than the literal decorator-context and disposal-environment shapes compiler emit builds, so previously compiling calls remain assignable.
rubrics.criterion: The repair does not narrow the declaration surface below what emitted code constructs: literal decorator-application context objects and literal disposal environments (the shapes compiler emit builds call sites with) remain assignable to the updated signatures, so no previously compiling call of the affected helpers stops compiling.
